skill.name: Writing Hookify Rules
skill.description: Creates and explains Hookify rules for monitoring commands, file edits, prompts, and completion checks with YAML frontmatter and regex patterns.
skill.summary: Write clear Hookify rules with suitable events, conditions, actions, patterns, and messages.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: All 116 static alerts are false positives caused by Markdown backticks and defensive regex examples. The skill contains documentation only and shows no prompt injection, secret access, destructive execution, or dynamic code execution.

static_findings.snippet: Hookify rules are markdown files with YAML frontmatter that define patterns to watch for and message
- `block`: Prevent operation (PreToolUse) or stop session (Stop events)
- YAML quoted strings: `"pattern"` requires double backslashes `\\s`

content.value_statement: Hookify rules can fail when events, conditions, or regex patterns are unclear. This skill guides users toward precise rules with useful warnings and blocks.
actual_capabilities: Creates Hookify rule files with required YAML frontmatter and Markdown messages.
Selects bash, file, stop, prompt, or all events for the requested behavior.
Builds simple regex patterns and advanced rules with multiple conditions.
Explains supported fields, operators, actions, naming, and file locations.
Suggests clear warning or blocking messages with practical alternatives.
Reviews regex scope and YAML escaping to reduce unwanted matches.
limitations: Does not install Hookify or confirm that the runtime is available.
Cannot guarantee regex accuracy without representative matching and nonmatching samples.
Guidance follows the documented syntax and may not reflect future Hookify changes.
Does not execute generated rules or inspect external example directories automatically.

use_cases.title: Prevent unsafe commands
use_cases.description: Create blocking rules for destructive shell commands while allowing normal development commands.

use_cases.title: Enforce completion checks
use_cases.description: Add stop rules that remind agents to run tests, builds, and documentation checks.

use_cases.title: Protect sensitive files
use_cases.description: Warn when edits target environment files, credentials, certificates, or other protected paths.

prompt_templates.title: Create a basic warning
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Hookify warning rule for console logging in TypeScript files. Explain the event, pattern, and message.

prompt_templates.title: Block a command pattern
prompt_templates.prompt: Write a Hookify rule that blocks recursive deletion commands. Include a focused regex and a safer alternative.

prompt_templates.title: Combine file conditions
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a file rule that warns when API key assignments are added to environment files. Use multiple conditions.

prompt_templates.title: Design a rule set
prompt_templates.prompt: Design three coordinated Hookify rules for command safety, production deployment prompts, and completion checks. Minimize false matches and explain tradeoffs.

output_examples.input: Warn when console logging is added to TypeScript files.
output_examples.output: A file-event rule using path and new-text conditions, followed by a message recommending the project logging library.
A bash-event rule with a focused recursive-deletion pattern, blocking action, and guidance to verify the target path.

output_examples.input: Require checks before the agent stops.
output: A stop-event rule that matches completion attempts.
A short checklist covering tests, build status, and documentation.

best_practices: Test patterns against examples that should match and examples that should not match.
Use narrow event types and conditions before choosing broad all-event rules.
Write messages that explain the risk and provide a practical next action.
anti_patterns: Do not use broad patterns that match unrelated commands, paths, or words.
Do not block operations when a warning provides enough protection.
Do not store local Hookify rules in version control without reviewing repository policy.

faq.question: What file format does Hookify use?
faq.answer: Rules are Markdown files with YAML frontmatter and a Markdown message body.

faq.question: Which events are supported?
faq.answer: The documented events are bash, file, stop, prompt, and all.

faq.question: Can a rule prevent an operation?
faq.answer: Yes. Use the block action for supported pre-operation or stop events.

faq.question: How do multiple conditions work?
faq.answer: Every listed condition must match before the rule triggers.

faq.question: Where should local rules be stored?
faq.answer: Store them under the project .claude directory using a descriptive hookify name ending in .local.md.

faq.question: How should regex patterns be tested?
faq.answer: Test representative positive and negative samples with Python-compatible regex behavior before enabling the rule.
